reviews.title: Expensive, Misleading, and Not Worth the Money
reviews.text:
Luxy markets itself as an exclusive dating platform for successful professionals, but my experience was disappointing from the beginning.

My profile was 100% complete, yet I was told I had only a 35% chance of approval, with the option to pay to bypass the review process. A genuine photograph of me was also rejected as supposedly not authentic.

The membership prices are outrageous: $119.99 for one month and nearly $600 for a year. For those prices, I would expect meaningful filtering options, transparency, and a genuinely exclusive experience.

I wanted to connect with established professionals within a specific age range, yet I was shown men significantly younger than my preferences. The profiles displayed impressive careers and income claims, but I saw no clear evidence that those financial claims were independently verified.

The constant pressure to upgrade, artificial sense of urgency, and limited functionality made the experience feel more like an aggressive sales strategy than a quality dating service.

I’m willing to pay for a worthwhile service, but exclusivity should mean something beyond an expensive subscription.

I deleted my account rather than pay for an experience that hadn’t earned my trust. Luxy needs to focus less on selling an image of luxury and more on delivering the quality, transparency, and functionality its pricing suggests.

reviews.title: Pressure into paying
reviews.text:
The review process feels intentionally designed to pressure users into paying. I completed 100% of my profile, verified my photos, filled out my bio and prompts, and have been getting significant profile traffic and engagement. During the initial review, the app showed my “chance of passing” increase as I completed my profile, but it appeared to cap at 50%. After waiting through the review period, I was told I hadn’t reached the approval threshold but was an “excellent applicant” deserving a secondary review and was placed on a waitlist for up to 14 days.

Almost immediately, I was repeatedly offered Luxy Black for $69.99/month to “skip the review,” including urgency-based discounts and messaging encouraging me to pay for immediate access. If I’m supposedly an excellent applicant and my profile is actively receiving traction, the constant paid shortcut makes the review process feel less like genuine quality control and more like a conversion tactic.

I’m willing to wait for the free review process, but consumers should have much more transparency about how acceptance decisions are made, what the displayed percentage actually represents, and whether purchasing a subscription affects access. There should be stronger consumer protections around apps using artificial scarcity, lengthy wait periods, or uncertainty to encourage expensive recurring subscriptions.

I’m not paying $70/month simply to bypass an approval process that the app itself says I’m a strong candidate for.

reviews.title: Luxury Price, Basic Experience
reviews.text:
I gave Luxy a full month, and it was a complete waste of time and money.

The membership is ridiculously expensive for an app that gives you very little visibility. Your age and dating preferences control who YOU see, but that does not mean Luxy is actually showing your profile to those people. If you want real activity, apparently paying for the membership isn’t enough, you’re expected to keep paying for Boosts just to be seen. So what exactly is the $120 membership paying for?

The app also constantly recycles the same profiles, including men you’ve already swiped left on.

And if you’re a woman over 35, think twice before spending your money here. From what I experienced, many of the older men on Luxy are specifically looking for women significantly younger than themselves. Some openly state in their bios that 35 is already “too old,” while being well past that age themselves. At least they make it clear upfront, so you know not to waste your time liking or swiping on them.

The dynamic also feels backwards. A lot of the men seem more interested in collecting attention, likes, charms and compliments than actually pursuing women. It often feels like they’re waiting to be approached and admired.

Luxy feels more like Instagram for men who want to display their vacations, cars and lifestyle than a serious luxury dating app. Endless travel photos, photo albums and charm collections. And when you see someone sitting on 1,000+ charms, take that as a hint: they probably aren’t ex

reviews.title: Beware. They don’t have a filtering system nor offer refunds.
reviews.text:
I signed up for the app after receiving a list of few sites to try from a friend. However, shortly after creating my profile, I noticed that the majority of the men displayed were located outside of the United States and were primarily seeking casual relationships. Additionally, many of the profiles shown were significantly younger than my preferred age range.

As I continued navigating the platform, I realized there was no option to filter matches based on relationship intentions, such as “long-term” or “serious.” This was concerning, as most dating apps offer filtering features that allow users to better align with their preferences.

Within the first 24 hours, I contacted customer support with two primary concerns:
	1.	Why I was charged $600 for a subscription when I intended to sign up for a monthly plan.
	2.	Whether there was an option to filter profiles by relationship goals or limit visibility from individuals seeking something different.

Support responded that these filtering features are not currently available, nor is there an option to restrict visibility from users with opposing intentions.
